summary: Client epoch salt drift causes per-request idempotency mismatch across worker processes
description: Issue summary: Customer reports duplicated external tool/function invocations after a client-side retry. Root cause appears to be per-process epoch salt divergence used in idempotency hashing. This causes the SDK to generate different idempotency keys for logically identical retry attempts when requests are routed from different worker processes, leading to at-most-once semantics breaking into at-least-once in the customer's orchestration.
impact: NimbusAI observed duplicated webhook posts and doubled billing events for long-running orchestration flows in their Dedicated environment. Approx 30 customer requests (0.02% of traffic) in us-east over the last 48 hours produced duplicate downstream side-effects. Customer flagged as dedicated tier and requires mitigation/fix.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy a Python web app behind gunicorn (pre-fork model) with 4 workers running the Redwood Python SDK (v1.12.3) and a background task that refreshes an epoch salt on token rotation.
2) Send multipart streaming request that triggers a long-running function/tool call and then force a client-side retry (simulate connection flake).
3) Observe server logs and downstream webhook receipts: some retries produced a different idempotency hash when served by a different worker process leading to duplicate external invocation.
4) Repeat under a Go client using the sdk-go equivalent and a load balancer that round-robins connections; similar duplicates intermittently observed.
logs:
[2026-03-09T21:12:03Z] worker-1 INFO outgoing request idempotency_key=epoch:2026-03-09T21:12:00Z:hash:7f3a...
[2026-03-09T21:12:03Z] worker-3 INFO outgoing retry idempotency_key=epoch:2026-03-09T21:12:01Z:hash:a9b2...
[2026-03-09T21:12:04Z] webhook-target INFO received request idempotency_token=epoch:2026-03-09T21:12:00Z:hash:7f3a...
[2026-03-09T21:12:04Z] webhook-target INFO received request idempotency_token=epoch:2026-03-09T21:12:01Z:hash:a9b2...
Note: two different epoch timestamps found for logically same client request sequence. Worker processes reported different salt epochs due to race during in-process refresh.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: SDK maintains an epoch-based salt in memory that is refreshed asynchronously (on token rotation or periodic refresh). In pre-fork servers (gunicorn) or multiprocess deployments, the salt refresh can occur at different times in different worker processes because it is not centrally coordinated. When a client retry hits a different worker (or a different process instance after a restart), the SDK uses a different salt in the idempotency hash and the server treats the retry as a new request.
Confirmed reproduction on a local dev cluster by instrumenting salt timestamps in the SDK. Observed salt values diverging across processes by 1-2 seconds during refresh windows.
Potential contributing factor: ephemeral session regeneration in the customer's auth middleware that triggers SDK salt refresh path more frequently than expected.
Cross-reference: linked SUP-912345 (token rotation mid-flight duplicate-funcall-go-stream).
mitigation_attempts: Applied temporary workaround with customer: 1) Configure the application to use a sticky connection policy so retries are more likely to hit the same worker. 2) Disable aggressive in-process salt refresh in their integration (set refresh interval to larger value) as a stop-gap. 3) Advised the customer to upgrade to SDK alpha that exposes a shared-file/redis-backed salt store for multi-process deployments; customer testing in staging passed initial smoke tests.
proposed_fix:
1) SDK change: make epoch salt refresh coordinated across processes in common server topologies (file/redis fallback in SDK, or allow explicit external salt provider). 2) Server-side: accept an alternate canonical idempotency header from clients (e.g., x-rw-idempotency-logical-id) to allow clients to supply a stable id across retries. 3) Update docs and quickstart guidance for gunicorn/pre-fork and k8s multi-replica patterns.
Engineering owner: Luis Romero. Target patch: sdk-python v1.13.0 and sdk-go v0.9.5.
resolution: Workaround provided and validated in staging. Engineering started a patch to add an optional redis-backed salt provider in SDKs. Patch PRs opened (see related_github_prs). Plan to ship SDK patch in next minor release; will follow with documentation updates and a short blog post describing multi-process idempotency considerations.
